title: Mostly timing, not the person: quoter 115's lower new-quote hit rate is largely explained by quoting in months when estimators had just left. Matched by month, the gap is about 3 points, in line with a full-time estimator's. The bigger lever is estimating coverage and quote turnaround.
conclusion: Observed: quoter 115 is an engineer, not an estimator, and is still employed. Estimators 108 (retired 2024-03-01) and 109 (resigned 2021-04-15) and engineers 114 (resigned 2018-02-23) and 113 (resigned 2021-05-07) have left (q276). Half of 115's new quotes (217 of 430, 0.505) fall in 14 months in which they sent 9 or more. Most of those months come right after a departure: 2018-03 and 2018-05, Apr-Oct 2021, and Mar-Apr 2024. Three do not: 2019-12, 2022-12 and 2023-08 (q300, q320). In those 14 months the other quoters won 0.187 with an average turnaround of 8.13 days. In the 58 months with no 115 quotes they won 0.272 with 5.13 days (q299). Against peers' quotes from the same calendar month, 115's gap is -0.031 (n=430, customer-clustered SE 0.017, z about -1.8), against the -0.071 that customer x year gave (q290, q312, q320; reproduced in q334). By customer x quarter it is -0.030 (n=331) (q290). On the month-matched measure 115 sits near full-time estimator 109 (-0.038, n=2,675) and below 108 (+0.033, n=4,223); 108 minus 109 is 0.071 (q290, q320, q334). In 2021, a third of 115's quotes (0.335), 115 matched peers month for month: 0.125 against an expected 0.119 (q315, q320). A smaller residual remains outside 2021: -0.049 month-matched (n=286, SE 0.025). It rests partly on 2022, when 115 won 2 of 37 (q305, q315). Turnaround predicts winning even against quotes from the same month: +0.078 for quotes sent in 0-2 days and -0.092 for 8-30 days (about 2,190 quotes per quintile, q317). Interpretation: the gap I first attributed to estimator 115 mostly comes from when they quoted. They covered quoting in the months after estimators left, when the whole shop quoted slowly and won less. The more useful finding is about coverage. When estimating capacity drops, quoting falls to non-estimators and turnaround slips, and slower quotes go with fewer wins. Valued at month-matched peer rates, 115's shortfall is 13.2 wins, or $158,802 of quoted value over 7.61 years: $20,872 a year (q312). That is quoted revenue, not margin, and much of it accrued when no estimator was available to send those quotes.

claims.text: Quoter roles from HR: 115 is an engineer and still employed. 108 (estimator) retired 2024-03-01, 109 (estimator) resigned 2021-04-15, 113 (engineer) resigned 2021-05-07, 114 (engineer) resigned 2018-02-23, 118 (sales) resigned 2022-04-20. Estimators 254 and 327 were hired 2021-09-21 and 2024-05-10.

In 14 months 115 sent 9 or more new quotes. Those months hold 217 of 115's 430 new quotes (0.505). In them, other quoters won 0.187 with an average turnaround of 8.13 days. In the 58 months with no 115 quotes, others won 0.272 with 5.13 days, a gap of 0.085. Of the 14 months, 2018-03/05, 2021-04 to 2021-10 and 2024-03/04 follow departures; 2019-12, 2022-12 and 2023-08 do not.

Peers matched by calendar month: 115 -0.031 (n=430, SE 0.019; customer-clustered SE 0.017 across 120 customers, z about -1.8). For comparison, customer x year gives -0.071 (n=389, clustered SE 0.022, z about -3.2) and customer x quarter -0.030 (n=331, SE 0.02).

Month-matched gaps for other quoters: 108 +0.033 (n=4,223), 109 -0.038 (n=2,675), 254 -0.021 (n=2,196), 327 +0.027 (n=847). 108 minus 109 is 0.071. With month x turnaround band, 115 is -0.041 and 109 -0.030; with month x segment, 115 is -0.031 and 109 -0.040.
Excluding 2021: customer x year -0.071 (n=263, SE 0.025); year-month -0.049 (n=286, SE 0.025).

Quote size doesn't explain the gap. Within customer x year cells, 115's quotes are smaller than peers' (log price -0.312, log hours -0.318, work centres -0.317, n=389), similar to 109 and 254. A customer x year x size-tercile cell leaves 115 at -0.062 (n=343).

The status data look sound. Every won new quote has a sales order and no non-won quote does, for every quoter. 115's validity window averages 30.1 days, like everyone else's. No expired, lost or no-award quote from 108/109/115/254/327 had its part ordered within 365 days. Every RFQ has exactly one quote, and 115 has no null statuses.
Turnaround against same-month quotes, by quintile (2,189-2,190 quotes each): 0-2 days +0.078, 2-4 days +0.041, 4-6 days +0.018, 6-8 days -0.045, 8-30 days -0.092. Raw hit rates are 0.342 to 0.131.
Sizing at month-matched peer rates: 13.2 missing wins, $158,802 of quoted value over 7.61 years, $20,872 a year. Under customer x year it was 27.7 wins, $257,449, $33,837 a year.

not_evidence_of: Not evidence that quoter 115 quotes badly or is at fault. They were an engineer covering quoting, mostly in months after estimators left, and their month-matched gap is in the same range as full-time estimator 109's. Not evidence that faster quoting causes wins: slow quotes may be harder or less wanted RFQs. The dollar figure is quoted revenue under an assumed peer win rate, not margin, and is largely not recoverable for months when no estimator was available. Departures and the low-win months coincide in time, but the records don't show that the departures caused the slowdown (2021 also had other conditions).
could_not_tell: Why quotes were lost: there is no loss reason or competitor price, and 'expired' means the buyer never replied. How RFQs are assigned between estimators and engineers, whether quotes were followed up, and whether 115 got the leftover or harder RFQs within a month. What drove the -0.049 residual outside 2021, which is about 2 SE and leans on 2022's 2 wins in 37. The standard errors don't account for uncertainty in the peer rates.
next_step: Treat estimating coverage as the issue. Track RFQ-to-quote turnaround and who sent each quote, month by month, and plan backfill or cross-training before an estimator leaves. Record an assignment reason and a loss reason when a quote's status is entered. If the remaining residual is worth checking, review a small sample of 115's 2022-2024 lost and expired new quotes next to same-month peer quotes for the same customer.
dead_ends: Higher markup or longer lead weeks at low-hit quoters: 115 is at +0.007 log markup and -0.44 lead weeks, and neither predicts winning within customer-year (q245, q248).
115 getting bigger or more complex RFQs: their quotes are smaller than peers', and a size cell leaves -0.062 (q279, q290).
Status recording or validity-window differences: none found (q281, q283, q286).
115 as a singular outlier: matched by month, they are no further below peers than estimator 109, and 108 minus 109 is 0.071 (q290, q320).
Estimator 118's low raw hit rate: explained by period and turnaround (q254, q259, q290).
response_to_challenge: Accepted on every point. I re-ran the month-matched comparison myself and it reproduces: 115 -0.031, 109 -0.038, 108 +0.033 (q334, matching q290). The challenger's other numbers come from queries they ran, which I cite. What I accepted: (1) My customer x year cell compared 115's quotes from the worst months of 2021 with peers' quotes from better months of the same year. Month matching halves the gap to -0.031, z about -1.8 with customer clustering (q290, q312). (2) 115 is an engineer covering quoting after estimators left (q276, q299, q300). (3) With timing controlled, 115 is not an outlier relative to 109, so my title's 'one estimator stays 6-7 points below peers' was wrong (q290, q320). (4) The dollar figure drops from $33,837 to $20,872 a year of quoted value, and that is not recoverable money (q312). What I kept: the status data are sound (q283, q286); quote size and price don't explain the gap (q279, q248); and turnaround's link to winning survives a same-month control (q317). I added one note: 3 of the 14 heavy-115 months (2019-12, 2022-12, 2023-08) don't follow a departure (q300), so the coverage story explains most of the clustering, not all of it. I still report the residual outside 2021 (-0.049, about 2 SE, q305) but don't treat it as a robust individual pattern.
